To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the primary response of the rabbit, to Salmonella typhi murium O antigens, includes a γG component, (2) γM-antigens are produced in the primary response, and (3) the primary response is characterized by a progressive increase in the avidity of anti-O antibody.
the primary response of rabbits to Salmonella typhi O antigen includes a γG component that is not detectable by standard methods.

the primary response of rabbits to Salmonella O antigens is characterized by a γG response, not detected by conventional assays, that is similar to that seen in animals stimulated by soluble antigens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an immunoglobulin-specific method for the quantitative analysis of the primary and the secondary immune response.
the development of a sensitive assay method for the measurement of the immunoglobulins of the antibody produced by the rabbit in the response to Salmonella typhi murium O antigens.
the development of an assay method that is sensitive to the production of all immunoglobulin classes and subclasses in response to a bacterial antigen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the methods employed are useful in the qualitative and quantitative analysis of the primary and anamnestic response of the rabbit, and that the methods employed can be used to demonstrate a secondary-type response to a somatic antigen.

the method of assay developed is capable of detecting the presence of γG- and/or γM-antigenic specificity and of quantitatively estimating the molar concentrations of these immunoglobulins in serum during the response to Salmonella typhi murium O antigens.
the method of assay is useful in the detection of γG-antiglobulin complexes, and in the determination of the minimal interval between the appearance of γM- and γG-antigen complexes in serum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method of assay is sensitive enough to detect the presence of γG-antiserum, but not to measure it.
the primary response of the rabbit is characterized by a γM-antigenic response, followed by a γG response.

the primary and secondary responses to Salmonella typhi murium O antigens are characterized by the production of both γM and γM immunoglobulins, the γG appearing earlier and in greater concentration than the γM in the primary response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the methods developed are sensitive enough to detect and quantify the immunoglobulin classes in the response to whole organism.
the methods described here provide a useful tool to study the kinetics of the antibody response to Salmonella typhi.
the methods developed are capable of detecting and quantifying both γG and γM antibodies to O antigens.
